qs.situation: A customer orders on Friday 20 December and you promise delivery in 5 working days. Christmas Day and New Year's Day fall inside that period.
options: Only Saturdays and Sundays are days off, so the holidays still count as working days
Saturdays, Sundays and national public holidays are days off
Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays and our own shop closure days are all days off

qs.situation: An order arrives on Saturday 14 June and the promise is '1 working day'.
options: Promised for Monday 16 June, with the count starting from the next working day
Promised for Tuesday 17 June, because Saturday orders are treated as received on Monday
Staff must pick the date by hand for weekend orders

qs.situation: A supplier's deadline is Wednesday and staff need the date 3 working days before it, to place the order in time.
options: Count backwards over working days only, which gives the previous Friday
Count backwards over every calendar day, weekends included, which gives the previous Sunday
Counting backwards is not allowed, only forward dates are given

qs.situation: A staff member types a birth date or order date that is impossible (30 February) or leaves it blank in a customer record, and a report is running.
options: A blank gives a blank result, while an impossible date stops the report with an error message
Both a blank and an impossible date give a blank result and the report carries on
Any blank or impossible date stops the whole report with an error message

qs.situation: A customer was born on 29 February 2000 and wants to buy an age-restricted item (18+) in a year with no 29 February.
options: They turn 18 on 1 March
They turn 18 on 28 February
Staff decide each case by hand

qs.situation: A $1,000 invoice is paid 60 days late.
options: 1.5% for every 30 days late, counted day by day, so $30 with no cap and no minimum
A single flat $25 fee, however many days late
2% for each month started, with a $10 minimum and a cap of 10% of the invoice

qs.situation: A student scores 89.5 out of 100 on a course.
options: B, because A starts at 90, with 80, 70 and 60 for B, C and D and no plus or minus grades
B+, because we use plus and minus grades
A, because we round up to the nearest whole mark, or our cut-offs are lower (for example A from 85)

qs.situation: A student scores 105 out of 100 thanks to bonus questions.
options: Gets an A, because bonus marks are fine
Gets an A, but the record is flagged for a teacher to check
No grade is given, because a score over the maximum is treated as a data entry mistake

qs.situation: A receipt is printed for the card 4111 1111 1111 1234.
options: Only the last 4 digits are shown, and every other digit is hidden
The first 6 and the last 4 digits are shown
Only the last 2 digits are shown

qs.situation: A cashier types a card number with dashes (4111-1111-1111-1234), or a number that is too short, or one that contains letters.
options: Dashes and spaces are ignored; a short number or one with letters is fully hidden
Dashes are kept in the printout; a short number or one with letters is fully hidden
Anything that is not a clean card number is refused and nothing is printed

qs.situation: A staff member enters a 120% discount by mistake on a $50 item.
options: The entry is refused with an error message
It is treated as 100% off, so the item is free
It is ignored and the item is sold at full price

qs.situation: A 2.3 kg parcel is going to zone B.
options: Charged as 3 kg, with partial kilograms rounded up, at a base fee plus a rate per kg (cheapest A, then B, then C)
Charged for exactly 2.3 kg
Charged by weight band: up to 1 kg, up to 5 kg and up to 10 kg, each at one flat price

qs.situation: A parcel is booked for delivery zone 'D', which has no rates, or a zone typed in lowercase ('b').
options: Lowercase is accepted; an unknown zone gives an error and no charge
Lowercase is accepted; an unknown zone is charged at the zone C rate
Lowercase is accepted; for an unknown zone the shipping charge is left blank so staff quote by hand

qs.situation: A customer wants to send an 80 kg item, or a very light 0.4 kg parcel.
options: No weight limit and no free shipping: the same formula applies to everything
Over 30 kg we do not ship it, and staff give a manual quote
Parcels under 0.5 kg ship free as a promotion

qs.situation: A product is titled 'Café Crème – 50% Off!' and needs a web address ending.
options: cafe-creme-50-off, lowercase with accents removed and symbols dropped
café-crème-50-off, keeping the accents
cafe-creme-50-percent-off, with the % sign spelled out

qs.situation: A product title is written entirely in Hindi script (or is just symbols), so no usable Latin letters are left.
options: The web address ending is left empty
The original script is kept in the web address ending
A generic word with a number is used instead, such as 'product-1234'

qs.situation: A product has three ratings: 5, 4 and 4 stars (average 4.33).
options: Shows 4.3, rounded to one decimal
Shows 4.5, rounded to the nearest half star
Shows 4 stars, rounded to a whole number

qs.situation: One product has ratings of 5, 4 and a glitch entry of 9 stars, and a second product has no ratings at all.
options: The glitch and blank entries are ignored, and a product with no ratings shows 'no rating yet'
The 9 is counted as 5 stars, and a product with no ratings shows 0 stars
A product with any invalid entry shows no headline rating until staff check it

qs.situation: A brand-new product has just one rating, a 5-star review from the owner's cousin.
options: Shows 5.0 stars straight away
Shows no headline rating until it has at least 5 ratings
Shows a figure pulled toward the shop's overall average, for example 4.2
